sample.task: Write dialogue from a scene from the animated teen series “Jane”, where Jane, her 12 year old friend and neighbour Molly-Rose Ling, and Molly-Rose’s 14 year old brother Aaron Ling hanging out when Molly-Rose starts talking about her childhood memories while speaking in Malay, which Jane doesn’t understand
sample.chosen:
Jane, Molly-Rose, and Aaron were hanging out in Jane's living room, chatting and laughing. Molly-Rose suddenly got a nostalgic look in her eyes and started speaking in Malay.

Molly-Rose: "Ahh, ingat kembali masa kecil, ketika kami bermain di taman. Kami bermain baling-baling dan sepak bola, dan Mama membuat kue kering untuk kami."

Jane looked at Molly-Rose, confused. "Uh, Molly-Rose, I didn't understand a word you just said."

Aaron chuckled and translated for his sister. "She's talking about our childhood memories, playing in the park, flying kites and playing soccer. She also mentioned how our mom used to make us cookies."

Jane smiled, "Oh, that sounds so fun! I wish I could understand Malay. Maybe you guys could teach me some words?"

Molly-Rose nodded eagerly, "Ya, saya boleh ajar kamu banyak perkataan dalam Bahasa Melayu!" (Yes, I can teach you many words in Malay!)

Aaron laughed, "She said yes, she can teach you many words in Malay."

And so, the three friends spent the rest of the afternoon learning and practicing Malay words, creating new memories together.

Title: "Nostalgic Chatter in Malay"

Scene: Jane, Molly-Rose, and Aaron are hanging out in their backyard. Molly-Rose starts reminiscing about her childhood.

Molly-Rose: (smiling) "Remember when we used to play 'teng-teng' in the mangrove forest? It was so much fun!"

Aaron: (laughs) "Yeah, those were the days. But what's 'teng-teng'?"

Jane: (confused) "I'm sorry, I don't understand. Is that a game?"

Molly-Rose: (smiling) "Oh, it's a game we played when we were kids. We'd make these little boats out of leaves and float them down the river. It was all about strategy and teamwork."

Jane: (intrigued) "That sounds interesting, but I'm still not sure what 'teng-teng' means."

Aaron: (smiling) "It's Malay for 'boat'. So, 'teng-teng' means 'leaf boat'."

Jane: (ah-ha moment) "Oh, I see! That's so cool. I've never heard of that game before."

Molly-Rose: (smiling) "It was a lot of fun. And we'd often sing songs while we played. Do you know any Malay songs, Jane?"

Jane: (thinking) "I don't think so, but I'd love to learn. It's fascinating to hear about your culture."

Aaron: (smiling) "Maybe we can teach you some songs next time. It's always good to learn new things."

Molly-Rose: (smiling) "That's a great idea, Aaron. Jane, it's been fun sharing these memories with you. I hope we can do more of this."

Jane: (smiling) "Absolutely, Molly-Rose. I've enjoyed learning about your culture. And I'm looking forward to those Malay songs."

The scene ends with laughter and a promise to learn more about each other's cultures.
